text:
maria: Heads-up: Customer 'Acme' escalated. Using /v1/rerank/batch and we got back responses where the per-query candidate lists don't align with scores — downstream consumer crashed (index out of range). Attached payload + response sample below.

alex: Can you paste the exact request body and the raw response?

maria: Here's a redacted example (they said this reproduces 100%):
```json
{
  "requests": [
    {"query_id": "q-1", "candidates": ["doc_a", "doc_b", "doc_c"]},
    {"query_id": "q-2", "candidates": ["doc_x", "doc_y"]}
  ]
}
```
Response body (200):
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"query_id": "q-1", "scores": [0.9, 0.7]},
    {"query_id": "q-2", "scores": [0.6, 0.4, 0.25]}
  ]
}
```

sam: Hmm odd ordering — looks like scores got shifted across queries. Are they using any client-side flattening or gzip chunked uploads?

maria: They POST from a Java client using okhttp + gzip. They said payload size ~12.3k. Request-id: req_20240312_ak47. Server logs snippet shows: 
```
ERROR rerank_service: ERR_MISMATCH candidate_count(5) != scores_len(3) req=req_20240312_ak47
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/redwood/runtime/rerank/handler.py", line 214, in handle_batch
    assert len(scores) == sum(len(r["candidates"]) for r in req["requests"])
AssertionError
```

jlee: I pulled the payload and ran a local repro. Repro steps:
1) Save the above JSON as body.json
2) curl -s -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" --data-binary @body.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' --compressed
I see the same mismatch when the gzip write boundary splits inside the candidates array — server's chunk reassembly logic incorrectly concatenates arrays instead of preserving per-query boundaries.

eng-bot: Created incident INC-5124 and notified eng-ml. Priority: P1 :rotating_light:

alex: Can we patch a server-side validation ASAP to 400 on mismatched lengths (rather than returning 200 with bad mapping)? Also add a sanity check to not merge arrays across requests during stream reassembly.

sam: Also seeing elevated latencies around the same timeframe (spikes to 1.2s 95th on rerank.batch). GC logs on worker-12 show increased compaction around 08:13 UTC. Might be correlated.

jlee: Temporary mitigation for the customer: either send each query as a separate /v1/rerank request (workaround) or include an explicit "per_query_counts" field: e.g. 
```json
{
  "requests": [...],
  "per_query_counts": [3,2]
}
```
Server will honor per_query_counts if present (we added a compatibility shim in the proxy for older clients).

maria: Customer is upset — they were charged for 12 failed/partial attempts. Asking for billing credit and ETA.

alex: Approving refund for failed calls. Eng-ml will push a hotfix to the streaming boundary handling (rollout window: 30m canary, then full). Patching validation first. Assigning to @jlee and @sam.

maria: Thanks — I'll notify Acme and provide the workaround + credit confirmation. :thumbsup:
